title: setup hook --absolute writes the quoted real path of the binary instead of the word jitso, and is idempotent
source: intended: docs/decisions.md D8 (setup hook, defect N-17): jitso registers its guard in the project's .claude/settings.json without clobbering anything
intent: INTENDED behavior (defect N-17, setup hook). `--absolute` writes `'<real path>' hook guard` (the dispatcher's quoting) in the four handlers and prints no PATH warning (the command is not the bare word). A second `--absolute` run is `nothing to do`; a plain run then rewrites the handlers to the bare word. Since N-25 the guard also has a third PreToolUse group, `Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit`. The oracle has no `setup` command: it answers `unknown command "setup"` on stderr with exit 2 and prints nothing on stdout, so every expectation that needs this output or file effect FAILS on it.

stdout: nothing to do (the guard is already registered in .claude/settings.json)
